about: The series the home page's curve draws (visual D-1). From the history register of the research pass (register.md and data.json, every number checked against its source on 2026-10-03). hack/website-chart.mjs draws it into index.html.

series.title: New repositories created on GitHub per year
series.definition: Repositories created in the Octoverse year (12 months ending ~Sep 30; Aug 31 for 2025). 2018 is derived (≈1/3 of 96M). 2026 is an annualised monthly rate, not a full-year total.
series.caveat: Do not plot the 2026 point as a completed year; mark it "annualised rate".

points.note: derived: "one third of all repositories were created in the last 12 months" x 96M
annualised: "new repositories per month rising to about 24M" x 12 (GitHub, Aug 2026)

latest_note_source: register.md §7: "Mark the 2026 point of github_new_repos_per_year as 'annualised August rate'."
caption: Linear scale. Sources: GitHub, its Octoverse reports of 2018 to 2025 and its blog posts of December 2013 and August 2026, and for 2023 a summary of the Octoverse report (altusintel.com).
latest_caption: The dotted end is a rate, not a year: about 24M new repositories in August 2026, times twelve.

figures.claim: new repositories on GitHub in Sep 2024–Aug 2025
figures.source: research register §1 #7 and §3.2: "121M new repos", Sep 2024–Aug 2025 (A); Octoverse 2025, https://github.blog/news-insights/octoverse/octoverse-a-new-developer-joins-github-every-second-as-ai-leads-typescript-to-1/

projection_note: The register gives no projection for this series. When it does, set projection to {"year", "value", "label": "If the curve holds", "caption": the sentence the caption adds, "figure": {"num", "claim"}}: hack/website-chart.mjs then draws the dashed line and writes its sentence and figure. Until then neither exists, and neither do the growth-since-the-inflection figure or the end-of-decade figure the deck asks for.
